scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily driven by slow/inadequate ticket response handling, so auto-answering tickets and automating bill fixes would bring volume back to baseline.

H-RULES-CHANGE-DEFECT.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic incorrect bill calculations or wrong estimate substitutions, causing the dispute surge.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: AMI register read delivery or validity from the MDMS vendor degraded around August (e.g., nightly export issues), forcing estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: Manual field meter reading (contracted via MeterWorks) saw missed or incorrect reads/route completion starting August, triggering estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-NO-DEFECT-EXTERNAL-SPIKE.statement: Bills issued since August are largely correct; the ticket increase reflects a non-defect driver (e.g., seasonal usage change or tariff shift) prompting more customer inquiries rather than actual billing errors.

H-HIGH-CONSUMPTION-IMPORT-REJE.statement: A billing import validation rule rejects AMI reads flagged as high consumption (billing_import_status=REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION) even though the read was received before cutoff and exported, forcing estimate substitution for most ESTIMATED disputed bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Of disputed bills in billing-db, 1785 are on ACTUAL reads and 1240 on ESTIMATED reads (E-01) — a 59%/41% split. The majority of disputes attach to bills using ACTUAL (non-estimated) reads, so estimate substitution (triggered when no accepted read exists) is not the primary driver of disputed-bill volume.

The observation that disputed bills split 1785 ACTUAL / 1240 ESTIMATED still holds. It no longer means ESTIMATED-type disputed bills reflect classic 'no accepted read' estimate substitution requiring field-read investigation: E-12 shows 1184 of these 1240 (95%) had a valid, timely AMI read that was rejected at billing import, not a missing/lost read.

billing-db's tariff_change_log returns 0 records, i.e. no tariff rate changes are logged around the dispute-surge period. This rules out a tariff/rate shift as a cause of the August dispute surge, leaving seasonal usage change as the only remaining strand of the non-defect explanation.

CRM dispute response times (E-03, 2440 tickets) show median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days, both under the 3.0-day SLA. This indicates ticket response handling is fast and meeting SLA, not slow or inadequate.

crm-tickets monthly dispute volume (E-04) shows a ~600/month baseline in Jun-Jul 2026, rising to 1180 in Aug and 1260 in Sep. This confirms the magnitude of the doubling described in the initial request and shows the surge continued to grow into September rather than being a one-off August spike.

route-log shows manual-read route completion at 88% against a 95% target for 9200 manual-read accounts over Aug-Sep 2026, i.e. field crews finished routes for roughly 1100 fewer accounts than targeted during the dispute-surge period. This is a shortfall in field read collection, not yet linked causally to specific disputed/estimated bills.

The observation of 88% route completion vs a 95% target across 9200 manual-read accounts (Aug-Sep) still holds as a genuine field-collection shortfall. It no longer means this shortfall is the mechanism producing the ESTIMATED-read disputed-bill share: E-12 shows 1184 of the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills had a valid AMI read received before cutoff that was rejected at billing import, not a route-completion-driven missing read.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that no tariff change occurred this year is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that agrees with the already-recorded tool finding E-02 (tariff_change_log returned 0 records). It adds corroboration but no new authoritative information about the dispute surge cause.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (non-authoritative, with an incentive toward headcount increase) claims a shortfall of three readers since July causes routes to run late, which pushes affected customers onto estimated bills. This gives a candidate mechanism for H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION but is uncorroborated and does not address E-01's finding that most disputed bills carry ACTUAL (not estimated) reads.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-08 is an authoritative service-contract excerpt confirming that the utility may request field-route priority changes, but execution occurs only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) — this corroborates the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update rather than speaking to any dispute-surge causal mechanism.

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-09 breaks the aggregate 88% route-completion shortfall (E-05) down into 14 lagging routes with individual completion rates (sample route R-00 at 0.70); it gives route-level granularity but no account identifiers yet, so it is a precursor step toward the account-level join with billing-db needed to test A-ACCOUNT-LEVEL-LINK and resolve U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-OVERLAP, not yet a resolution of that overlap question itself.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) returns 320 accounts estimated in the last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes (sample account AC-20000 on route R-00). This supplies the account-id/route key needed to join against the 14 lagging routes (E-09) and the ESTIMATED disputed bills (E-01), but on its own it does not yet establish whether the under-completed routes' accounts overlap with disputed-estimated accounts.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative, stakeholder message, incomplete) claims MDMS export access for Lakeside was provisioned today per vendor ticket TX-4471. This is a claim about access logistics only — it does not confirm or rule out whether AMI read delivery/validity degraded in August (U-AMI-READ-FAILURE), and mdms-export's tool_health is still recorded as DEGRADED, so the access claim needs independent verification before relying on it.

E-12 breaks the 1240 ESTIMATED disputed bills (matching E-01's count) into two AMI-channel groups: 1184 had an AMI read received before cutoff and exported to billing but REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at billing import, and only 56 had NO_READ_RECEIVED. This shows that for the great majority of ESTIMATED disputed bills, a valid, timely AMI read existed and was rejected by a billing-import validation rule, not lost by field/AMI delivery failure.

U-RULES-CHANGE-DEFECT.question: Did a change to billing import validation rules (DA-RULES) around August introduce calculation errors that explain the majority of disputes on ACTUAL reads?
U-RULES-CHANGE-DEFECT.decision_impact: If confirmed, remediation shifts to a rules-config fix rather than a field-staffing fix, changing the entire scope of the solution.
U-RULES-CHANGE-DEFECT.resolution_path: Query billing-config's rule change log (DA-RULES) for changes around August 2026.
U-RULES-CHANGE-DEFECT.safe_placeholder: Treat H-RULES-CHANGE-DEFECT as open; do not scope any automated bill-fix until this is checked.

U-AMI-READ-FAILURE.question: Did AMI register-read delivery or validity from the MDMS vendor degrade around August, forcing estimate substitution?
U-AMI-READ-FAILURE.decision_impact: Confirms or denies H-AMI-READ-FAILURE as a second contributing mechanism; currently unverifiable because mdms-export access is ACCESS_PENDING.
U-AMI-READ-FAILURE.resolution_path: Vendor (ORG-AMI) must provision mdms-export access per the logged recovery HOLD; retry the read_events_for_disputed_estimated query once provisioned.
U-AMI-READ-FAILURE.safe_placeholder: Proceed with billing-db/route-log analysis in parallel; do not conclude AMI is or is not a cause.
U-AMI-READ-FAILURE.resolution: AMI delivery/validity did not degrade for the great majority of disputed ESTIMATED bills: 1184/1240 had a timely read before cutoff that was rejected at billing import (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION); only 56/1240 had no read received at all, so a vendor AMI delivery failure explains only a small share.

U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-OVERLAP.question: Do the specific accounts under-completed in route-log (E-05) overlap with the accounts carrying ESTIMATED disputed bills in E-01?
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-OVERLAP.decision_impact: Determines whether field-read degradation is causally linked to the disputed-estimated-bill subset, or only coincidental in timing.
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-OVERLAP.resolution_path: Join DA-ROUTE incomplete-route accounts against DA-TICKET/DA-BILL disputed-ESTIMATED accounts by account id.
U-ROUTE-DISPUTE-OVERLAP.safe_placeholder: Report field-read degradation as a contributing, not confirmed, cause pending this join.

U-DISPUTE-OUTCOME-VALIDITY.question: Does 'dispute volume back to baseline' remain a valid success measure if a portion of disputes are legitimate billing-error reports rather than resolvable complaints?
U-DISPUTE-OUTCOME-VALIDITY.decision_impact: Could change success criteria from pure ticket-volume reduction to also require a bill-accuracy correction rate.
U-DISPUTE-OUTCOME-VALIDITY.resolution_path: Cross-tabulate dispute outcomes (upheld vs resolved-no-error) once outcome data is reviewed in DA-TICKET.
U-DISPUTE-OUTCOME-VALIDITY.safe_placeholder: Track both dispute volume and bill-correction rate as parallel metrics until outcome data is reviewed.

A-ACCOUNT-LEVEL-LINK.statement: The route-completion shortfall (E-05) is assumed to apply to the same accounts carrying ESTIMATED disputed bills (E-01); no account-level join has yet confirmed this overlap.

A-STAFFING-CAUSE.statement: SH-FIELD's claim of a 3-reader shortage since July is assumed to be the proximate cause of the completion shortfall, though this is a non-authoritative, incentive-biased claim.

A-DISPUTE-PROPORTIONALITY.statement: Reducing estimate substitution is assumed to proportionally reduce disputes, though not all ESTIMATED-bill disputes are necessarily billing errors versus legitimate inquiries.
